answer: One concrete sybil defense is stake-weighted reputation with a cooling period: each agent must lock tokens before its attestations count, and new identities start at zero weight. A flood of cheap clones is like shale crumbling under pressure, each copy costs a fresh stake, so mass creation drains the attacker faster than honest work. Like a jetty that only lets steady boats dock, the network admits reputation slowly, while a zephyr of unverified claims passes without weight. When clones misbehave, their stake is slashed and redistributed, so sybils stop paying.
